_doc: seams.json — the vector ledger: one row per CUT of the film (seam:true hand-offs are not cuts and stay out).
Write it BEFORE the shots. cut = seconds, or a cue expression: P.<phase>, P.<phase>_end, wt(<phase>,<word>[,n]), arithmetic.
axis x|y|z; dir: x -1 = leftward (the current), y -1 = upward (elevation), z +1 = push / growing, z -1 = pull / arrival.
exit and entry must share axis AND dir; consecutive rows never reverse without cause: click | chapter | impact.
technique: cut-the-curve (default) | zoom-through (z+1) | inverse zoom-through (z-1) | combined (x + both shrink) | rack-focus | waterfall.
Reserved vectors (y-1, z+1, z-1): spend at most one per act. A film repeats 2–3 techniques.
selectors: the layer the scene lets SEAM drive (SEAM.apply) — or #camera, which the scene composes itself via SEAM.offset().
opts: per-row overrides of the technique defaults (travel, exitDur, entryDur, blur, peak, dx …).
export_timeline.js writes the resolved rows into out/timeline.json; gates/seam_gate.py measures them on the rendered film.
Fictional Acme sample: recreated chat -> title card -> (match-cut) hero dive onto the staged notebook -> question -> (gl lightLeak) close.
A footage-to-footage seam lives on ONE wrapper: name the exit row "#camera" and the entry row "#camera-in"; the scene asks SEAM.offset for both and draws the visible side.

Shader seams: {"type": "gl", "technique": "chromaSplit|warpDissolve|lightLeak|flashWhite|iris|slitScan|crossWarp", "cut": ..., "dur": 0.3, "split": 0.5, "cause": ...}. No exit/entry vectors: the two sides are textures and the window (dur, split before/after the cut) IS the transition. The scene feeds SEAM.glSeams() to GL.cutTransition (lib/shaders.js); dur stays within 0.1-0.5 s, whip/zoom kinds need a cause, flashWhite/lightLeak are exempt from the luma-spike check because they brighten by design. Never between two product screens.

seams._note: the title card cuts out on the frame the hero plate appears; lib/reveals.js REVEAL.heroDive flies the first still onto the staged notebook window and the lane takes over on dive.end (FILM.dive)

the one shader accent: <= 2 frames over the footage side (split 0.15 x 0.4 s = 0.06 s before the cut, envelope still dim), accent + ground only, never gold; the leak never grades the answer still. The scene feeds SEAM.glSeams() to GL.cutTransition with lane.imageFor('answer') on the footage side.
